page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.1-16 is a memory-dense virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture within OCI's flexible Standard infrastructure family. The instance is provisioned with 1 dedicated physical core from an AMD EPYC 7742 processor, operating with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 2 vCPUs at a nominal clock frequency of 2.25 GHz. This compute configuration provides dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared or burstable time-slicing, ensuring consistent instruction processing.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that classifies it within memory-optimized parameters. Hardware tradeoffs are present in the I/O and acceleration subsystems: the profile includes no bundled local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely on remote block storage solutions. In addition, the instance contains zero GPUs, restricting processing exclusively to CPU pipelines. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the decoupled core-to-memory configuration allows operators to scale RAM independently of compute count, avoiding expenditures on unneeded processor cycles when a workload only requires a larger memory footprint. However, environments characterized by heavy disk I/O or vector acceleration may face performance constraints given the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators. VM.Standard.E3.Flex.1-16 is functionally aligned with lightweight database instances, in-memory caching tiers such as small Redis deployments, containerized application runtimes, and auxiliary ETL jobs that demand higher memory density than processing throughput.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.1-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration belonging to the Standard server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance pairs 1 dedicated physical core, providing 2 multithreaded vCPUs running at a base clock of 2.25 GHz, with 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields an expansive memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for persistent data, and features no hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. This resource profile offers cost-effective execution for entry-level workloads requiring substantial memory relative to compute capacity, mitigating over-provisioning of CPU cores. It is technically appropriate for mid-sized relational database replicas, in-memory caching layers, background data ingestion workers, and memory-intensive microservices.
